title: Proration of Superhost Response Rates over Suspension Days — Host Accounts
content:
# Programme Analytics Note — Proration of the Response Rate over Suspension Days (Host Accounts)

When the Superhost assessment of an individual Host Accounts holder is decided again after a suspension, the response rate taken for the decided assessment is worked out by one of three methods.

## Rule

1. For an account whose most recent suspension lasted **at least 14 calendar days**, and that had a policy strike overturned on a policy strike appeal approved within the 12 months before the decision, the decided assessment's response rate is the recorded response rate prorated to the lookback days outside the suspension: the recorded rate multiplied by 365 (the Superhost lookback, in calendar days), divided by 365 less the suspension days that fall inside the assessment's lookback, and never more than 100.
2. For an account whose most recent suspension lasted **at least 1 but fewer than 14 calendar days**, and that had a policy strike overturned in the same way, the recorded rate is prorated in the same way over only the suspension days inside the lookback beyond the first 3: the recorded rate multiplied by 365, divided by 365 less those suspension days in excess of 3 (nothing is taken off when there are 3 or fewer), and never more than 100.
3. For every other account no proration applies.

Each prorated rate is rounded half up to 2 decimal places.

## Terms used in the rule

- **Length of the most recent suspension**: the calendar days counted from its suspended date to the date its account suspension appeal was approved.
- **Suspension days inside the assessment's lookback**: the days counted from the suspended date to the assessment date, and never more than the length of the suspension; there are none when the assessment date is not after the suspended date.
- **Within the 12 months before the decision**: dated fewer than 12 whole calendar months before the date of the decision. The overturned strike is read from the decision date of the approved policy strike appeal.

## Which method — at a glance

| Most recent suspension lasted | Policy strike overturned on an appeal approved in the 12 months | Method |
|---|---|---|
| 14 days or more | Yes | 1 — every suspension day inside the lookback |
| 1 to 13 days | Yes | 2 — only the days beyond the first 3 |
| Any length | No | No proration |
| Never suspended | Yes or no | No proration |

## Worked figures (hypothetical accounts)

**Method 1.** Suspended 20 May, account suspension appeal approved 25 June: the suspension lasted 36 days. The decided assessment is dated 1 July, 42 days after the suspended date, so the suspension days inside its lookback are 36 (never more than the length of the suspension). One policy strike was overturned on an appeal approved in March of the same year. Recorded response rate 84.00%: 84.00 multiplied by 365, divided by 329, is 93.1915, rounded to **93.19%**.

**Method 2.** Suspended 22 June, appeal approved 30 June: the suspension lasted 8 days, and 8 suspension days fall inside the lookback of an assessment dated 1 July. Beyond the first 3, 5 days remain. Recorded rate 86.50%: 86.50 multiplied by 365, divided by 360, is 87.7014, rounded to **87.70%**.

**The ceiling.** A recorded rate of 98.00% with 60 suspension days inside the lookback under Method 1 gives 98.00 multiplied by 365, divided by 305, which is 117.28; the rate taken is **100.00%**.
